Grow Guide

Beginners Grow Guide

Growing your first plant is simpler than it looks. Eight basic steps, in order, from seed to jar — no experience needed, and no fancy gear beyond a pot, soil and a light.

Before you start: only grow where it is legal, and only if you are 21 or over. Rules differ by state — check yours in Laws by State below. This guide is general information, not legal advice.

1 Know the rules first

Only grow where home growing is legal. In New York, adults 21+ can grow up to 3 mature and 3 immature plants per person at home. Keep plants out of public view, and locked away from kids and pets.

Tip: Plant limits and rules change — check your state before you plant, not after.

2 Pick easy seeds

Start with feminized seeds — they grow into female plants, the kind that make buds — or autoflowers, which flower on their own timer without light changes. Both forgive beginner mistakes.

Tip: Shorter, indica-leaning plants are the easiest to manage indoors.

3 Germinate: the paper-towel trick

Fold your seeds inside a damp paper towel — damp, not dripping — and keep it somewhere warm and dark. Check daily. In 1–3 days a little white root tip pops out. Plant it root-down, about a knuckle deep in soil.

Tip: Handle the sprouted seed gently, by the shell — the baby root breaks easily.

4 Pot it in good soil

Use a 3–5 gallon fabric pot and light, fluffy potting soil with perlite (the little white bits). Fabric pots drain well, let roots breathe, and make overwatering much harder to do.

Tip: Whatever pot you use, it must have drainage holes in the bottom.

5 Give it lots of light

An LED grow light is the one bit of gear worth buying. While the plant is growing leaves, run it 18 hours on, 6 hours off. Hang it close above the plant, but never touching it.

Tip: A cheap plug-in timer does the remembering for you.

6 Water gently, feed lightly

Water only when the top inch of soil feels dry. Pour slowly until a little runs out of the bottom, then empty the saucer. If you use plant food, use half the strength on the bottle.

Tip: More first plants are killed by overwatering — love — than by anything else.

7 Flower time

When you're ready, switch the light to 12 hours on, 12 hours off — that tells the plant to make buds. Buds build over about 8–10 weeks. Check the trichomes (the frosty crystals) with a magnifier: milky white, with a few turning amber, means ready.

Tip: Autoflowers skip this step — they flower on their own schedule.

8 Harvest, dry, cure

Cut the branches and hang them in a dark, breezy room for about a week, until the small stems snap instead of bend. Trim the buds into glass jars, and open the jars once a day for the first couple of weeks to let moisture out.

Tip: Patience here is the whole difference between harsh and smooth.

That's a whole first grow: law, seeds, sprout, pot, light, water, flower, jar. Start with one or two plants, keep notes on what you did, and the second grow gets easier. Happy growing — and check the New York and California tabs for what's happening in the legal markets.
